translations.source_sense_description: kaputtgehen (wenn es dabei Splitter oder Brocken erzeugt)

glosses: To separate into two or more pieces, to fracture or crack, by a process that cannot easily be reversed for reassembly.

examples.text: If the vase falls to the floor, it might break.
In order to tend to the accident victim, he will break the window of the car.

First, marinate the tofu. In a bowl, whisk the kecap manis, chilli sauce, and sesame oil together. Cut the tofu into strips about 1cm thick, mix gently (so it doesn't break) with the marinade and leave in the fridge for half an hour.

glosses: To separate into two or more pieces, to fracture or crack, by a process that cannot easily be reversed for reassembly.
To crack or fracture (bone) under a physical strain.

examples.text: His ribs broke under the weight of the rocks piled on his chest.
He slipped on the ice and broke his leg.

glosses: To divide (something, often money) into smaller units.

examples.text: Can you break a hundred-dollar bill for me?
The wholesaler broke the container loads into palettes and boxes for local retailers.

glosses: To cause (a person or animal) to lose spirit or will; to crush the spirits of.

examples.text: Her child’s death broke Angela.
Interrogators have used many forms of torture to break prisoners of war.

If I had called, and had answered me, yet would I not beleeue that he had hearkened vnto my voice: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

glosses: To cause (a person or animal) to lose spirit or will; to crush the spirits of.

examples.text: Colonel: See, gentlemen? Any horse could be broken.

glosses: To be crushed, or overwhelmed with sorrow or grief.

examples.text: My heart is breaking.

glosses: To interrupt; to destroy the continuity of; to dissolve or terminate.

examples.text: I’ve got to break this habit I have of biting my nails.
to break silence; to break one's sleep; to break one’s journey
I had won four games in a row, but now you've broken my streak of luck.
Go, release them, Ariel; / My charms I'll break, their senses I'll restore.

glosses: To interrupt; to destroy the continuity of; to dissolve or terminate.
To end the run of (a play).

examples.text: In July Alexander broke the run and went on tour, as was his custom. He believed in keeping in touch with provincial audiences and how wise he was!
After Camberwell he broke the play's season and brought it back in the autumn with a few revisions and a noticeably strengthened cast but without any special success.

glosses: To ruin financially.

examples.text: The recession broke some small businesses.
With arts like these rich Matho, when he speaks, / Attracts all fees, and little lawyers breaks.

glosses: To fail in business; to go broke, to become bankrupt.

examples.text: He that puts all upon adventures doth oftentimes break, and come to poverty.
‘I knew he was in some such low way—He broke did not he?’

glosses: Of prices on the stock exchange: to fall suddenly.

examples.text: With a few exceptions, stock prices tend to follow the overall market averages. When you have a market decline, therefore, many stocks share the same overall chart pattern. Prices break and go sideways for a period of time.

glosses: To violate; to fail to adhere to.

examples.text: When you go to Vancouver, promise me you won't break the law.
He broke his vows by cheating on his wife.
to break one’s word

Out, out Hyæna; theſe are thy wonted arts, [...] To break all faith, all vows, deceive, betray,

glosses: To go down, in terms of temperature, indicating that the most dangerous part of the illness has passed.

examples.text: Susan's fever broke at about 3 AM, and the doctor said the worst was over.

glosses: To end.

examples.text: The forecast says the hot weather will break by midweek.

glosses: To begin or end.

examples.text: We ran to find shelter before the storm broke.
Around midday the storm broke, and the afternoon was calm and sunny.

glosses: To arrive.

examples.text: Morning has broken.
The day broke crisp and clear.
The day begins to break, and night is fled.

glosses: To render (a game) unchallenging by altering its rules or exploiting loopholes or weaknesses in them in a way that gives a player an unfair advantage.

examples.text: Changing the rules to let white have three extra queens would break chess.
I broke the RPG by training every member of my party to cast fireballs as well as use swords.

glosses: To stop, or to cause to stop, functioning properly or altogether.

examples.text: On the hottest day of the year the refrigerator broke.
Did you two break the trolley by racing with it?

glosses: To stop, or to cause to stop, functioning properly or altogether.
To cause (some feature of a program or piece of software) to stop functioning properly; to cause a regression.

examples.text: Adding 64-bit support broke backward compatibility with earlier versions.

glosses: To cause (a barrier) to no longer bar.

examples.text: to break a seal

glosses: To cause (a barrier) to no longer bar.
To cause the shell of (an egg) to crack, so that the inside (yolk) is accessible.
To cause (a barrier) to no longer bar.

examples.text: The cavalry were not able to break the British squares.

glosses: To collapse into surf, after arriving in shallow water.

examples.text: There are many places on the reef that break during the summer.

glosses: To burst forth; to make its way; to come into view.

examples.text: The Clouds are ſtill above; and, while I ſpeak, / A ſecond deluge o'er our head may break.

glosses: To interrupt or cease one's work or occupation temporarily; to go on break.

examples.text: Let's break for lunch.

glosses: To interrupt (a fall) by inserting something so that the falling object does not (immediately) hit something else beneath.

examples.text: He survived the jump out the window because the bushes below broke his fall.

glosses: To disclose or make known an item of news, a band, etc.

examples.text: Like the crash of thunderbolts…, the sound of musquetry broke over the lawn, ….

glosses: To change a steady state abruptly.

glosses: To (attempt to) disengage and flee to; to make a run for.

examples.text: As the last firing of the big guns begins to die down, the German light forces still fighting to the west begin to make their choices. Some break for the open sea; others run for the German-occupied coast; still others stand and die. A small group decide to strike their colors, in imitation of three of the larger German ships.

glosses: To suddenly become.

examples.text: Things began breaking bad for him when his parents died.

glosses: To become deeper at puberty.

examples.text: His voice breaks when he gets emotional.

glosses: To de-emulsify.

examples.text: Conversely, as the emulsion breaks and the system returns to the original state, energy is released.

glosses: To surpass or do better than (a specific number); to do better than (a record), setting a new record.

examples.text: He broke the men's 100-meter record.

examples.text: He needs to break serve to win the match.

glosses: To end (a connection); to disconnect.

examples.text:
M. Eyssette hausse les épaules :
— Si c’est Jacques qui y va, dit-il, la cruche est cassée, c’est sûr.
— Tu entends, Jacques, — c’est madame Eyssette qui parle avec sa voix tranquille, — tu entends, ne la casse pas, fais bien attention.
M. Eyssette reprend :
— Oh ! tu as beau lui dire de ne pas la casser, il la cassera tout de même.
Ici, la voix éplorée de Jacques :
— Mais enfin, pourquoi voulez-vous que je la casse ?
— Je ne veux pas que tu la casses, je te dis que tu la casseras, répond M. Eyssette, et d’un ton qui n’admet pas de réplique.
